blocks.tk: Dutar türkmen sazynyň esasy guralydyr. Onuň ady pars dilinden gelýär we “iki sim” diýmekdir. Dutaryň iki simi, uzyn sapy we armyt şekilli göwresi bar. UNESKO-nyň maglumatyna görä, ussalar onuň göwresini we ýuka ýüzüni tut agajyndan, sapyny bolsa erik agajyndan ýasaýarlar. Soňra ussa sapa perdeleri we simleri dakýar, dutary sazlaýar. Dutar ýasamak uly ussatlyk talap edýär: ussa agajy saýlamagy, kesmegi we bölekleri birleşdirmegi gowy bilmeli. Bu hünär köplenç atadan ogla geçýär.
blocks.en: The dutar is the heart of Turkmen music. Its name comes from Persian and means **two strings**: it is a long-necked lute with two strings and a pear-shaped body covered by a thin wooden soundboard. According to UNESCO, makers carve the body and the soundboard from mulberry wood and the neck from the dried trunk of an apricot tree; the soundboard is baked to drive out its moisture and fixed with bone glue, and then come the frets, the strings and the tuning. The craft has traditionally passed from father to son.

blocks.tk: Dutar türkmen durmuşynda hemme ýerde bar: toýlar we baýramlar dutarsyz geçmeýär. Dutary türkmen sazynyň ähli esasy görnüşlerinde ulanýarlar. Dutar sazynyň iki görnüşi bar. Birinjisinde sazanda dutary ýeke özi çalýar, oňa dutarçy diýýärler. Ikinjisinde bagşy dutar çalyp, aýdym aýdýar. Käbir bagşylar diňe uzyn dessanlary aýdýarlar.
blocks.en: No Turkmen wedding or holiday is complete without the dutar, which UNESCO calls part of all the main genres of Turkmen music. Its description of the tradition distinguishes two kinds of dutar music: tunes played on the instrument alone, the art of the *dutarçy*, and songs sung to the dutar, the art of the *bagşy*. One kind of bagşy specializes in epics, performing long *dessans* that mix narration, singing and improvisation.

blocks.tk: Bagşy diňe aýdymçy däl. Ol uzyn dessanlary ýatdan bilýär. Käbir dessanlary aýtmak üçin sagatlar gerek. Dessany aýdanda, ol käte gürrüň berýär, käte aýdym aýdýar. Bagşylar “Görogly” ýaly dessanlary we Magtymgulynyň, Keminäniň goşgularyny aýtmagy gowy görýärler. Demirgazykda bagşynyň ýanynda köplenç gyjakçy bolýar, günortada bolsa bagşy bir ýa-da iki dutar bilen çykyş edýär. Iki sebitiň aýdym aýdyş usuly hem başga. Dessanyň dowamynda bagşy dutaryny birnäçe gezek has ýokary sazlaýar, şeýdip aýdymyň güýji barha artýar.
blocks.en: A bagşy is more than a singer: he or she keeps the *dessans*, epic tales known by heart and told for hours, switching between speech and song. The repertoire runs from epics such as *Görogly* to songs on poems by Magtymguly and Kemine, two poets you will meet in the next two units. In the account published by The Culture Trip, northern bagşys perform with the *gyjak*, a bowed spike fiddle, while in the south the singer is accompanied by one or two dutars; the two regions also sing differently, the north in a throaty style, the south in a broad, high voice, and in both the singer retunes the dutar higher at each stage of a performance as the emotion rises. Britannica notes that after the Russian conquest in the late 19th century the Turkmen classics passed largely into the hands of the bagşys, who sang them to the dutar and the gyjak.

blocks.tk: Bagşy bolmak üçin köp ýyl okamak gerek. Ýaş şägirt halypanyň ýanynda ýaşap, ondan öwrenýär: halypasynyň çalyşyny diňleýär we dessanlary ýatdan öwrenýär. Okuwy gutaranda halypa şägirdine pata berýär. Rowaýata görä, bagşylaryň piri Aşyk Aýdyň pirdir, onuň mazary Daşoguz welaýatynda. Ýaş bagşylar onuň mazaryna zyýarata barýarlar.
blocks.en: The art is handed down from master to pupil. The apprentice, the *şägirt*, lives and learns beside a *halypa*, a master, for years, listening to him play and learning the dessans by heart; at the end, in the accounts gathered by The Culture Trip, the master presents the new bagşy to the community with a blessing, the *pata*. Legend names patron saints of the bagşys, among them Aşyk Aýdyň Pir, whose shrine in Dashoguz province young performers visit to ask for his blessing.

blocks.tk: 2021-nji ýylyň dekabrynda UNESKO türkmen dutaryny ýasamak we onuň bilen aýdym aýtmak sungatyny Adamzadyň maddy däl medeni mirasynyň sanawyna girizdi. Öň bagşylar köplenç erkek kişiler bolupdyr, häzir bolsa zenan bagşylar hem meşhur. Ýaşlar dutar çalmagy sungat mekdeplerinde we halypalaryndan öwrenýärler. Dutar ussalary hem hünärini ýaşlara öwredýärler.
blocks.en: In December 2021, at its 16th session, UNESCO's intergovernmental committee inscribed Turkmenistan's “Dutar making craftsmanship and traditional music performing art combined with singing” on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. The bagşys of the past were mostly men; today women are among the best-known performers. Young musicians learn both in schools of music and art and, as before, from a master, and dutar makers train apprentices of their own.

blocks.tk: Dutary ýasamak, ony çalmak we onuň bilen aýdym aýtmak bir sungatyň bölekleridir. Türkmenler bu sungaty köp asyrdan bäri saklaýarlar. Ol Türkmenistanyň ähli welaýatlarynda ýaşaýar.
blocks.en: Making the dutar, playing it and singing to it are, in UNESCO's description, parts of a single tradition, one the Turkmen have kept alive for centuries and which, according to the nomination file, is practised in every province of the country.

blocks.title: Reading the Turkmen
blocks.text: Look for this unit's verbal nouns: *dutar ýasamak* (making a dutar) as a subject, *agajy saýlamagy, kesmegi … birleşdirmegi* after *bilmeli*, *aýtmagy gowy görýärler*, *bagşy bolmak üçin* (in order to become a bagşy), and the `-(Y)ş` nouns *çalyş* (playing) and *aýdyş* (way of singing).
